title.narrative: Denmark's contribution to the UN Special Fund of the Optional Protocol to the Convention against Torture (OPCAT) 2022-2023.

description.narrative: The Special Fund for OPCAT is a unique mechanism of torture prevention and the only operational fund established by an international human rights treaty. Its support to national preventive mechanisms (NMS), the establishment of which is a core obligation under the Optional Protocol to the Convention against Torture is key in preventing torture at the national level. The main objective of the development cooperation is effective prevention of torture through supporting projects contributing to the establishment or strengthening of NPMs in developing countries in accordance with OPCAT and recommendations of the SPT or through the support of their education programmes.

title.narrative: Support for National Preventive Mechanisms (NPMs) that contributes to the torture prevention at the national level.
Number of projects supported to implement recommendations made by the Subcommittee for Prevention of Torture and other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment (SPT).

actual.value: 18 projects supported in 16 eligible States (Argentina, Benin, Bolivia, Chile, Hungary, Kazakhstan, Maldives, Mexico, Niger, Peru, the Philippines, the Republic of Moldova, Senegal, Spain, South Africa and Togo).

title.narrative: NPM’s collaboration with stakeholders (government authorities, penitentiary authorities, civil society organizations, professional groups – lawyers, judges, prosecutors, public defenders, social workers, psychologists and psychiatrists, medical doctors, religious leaders, journalists, other monitoring bodies, Parliamentarians) has increased, as well as visibility of NPMs and awareness of torture prevention.

Number of meeting with stakeholders, number of collaboration frameworks developed, number of public meetings, campaigns and emissions, number of NPM annual reports produced and disseminated; number of translation of NPM annual reports in the country languages; number of leaflets, posters, brochures produced and disseminated, including in the places of detention.

target.value: At least 20 meetings with stakeholders conducted, information documents on NPM produced and disseminated in at least five countries, annual NPM reports produced and disseminated; at least one public awareness campaigns on NPMs and torture prevention conducted, NGO observatory for torture prevention operationalized at least in in one country; a tool on prevention of self-inflicted violence and suicide of juveniles in places of detention produced.

actual.value: More than 15 meetings, roundtable discussions and conferences were organized through the projects for various stakeholders.

title.narrative: Knowledge and skills of NPM members and other stakeholders in torture prevention have increased.

Number of training activities on international standards, reporting and monitoring techniques (including gender sensitive monitoring); number of study visits and peer-learning activities among NPMs; number of monitoring visits with an expert support, number of tools and guidance on international standards available.

target.value: At least 15 training activities and workshops executed, at least two study visits/peer learning activities conducted; tools on understanding on international standards on torture prevention developed and replicated; monitoring visits to places of detention conducted in at least four countries.

actual.value: More than 15 training activities executed to increase knowledge and skills of NPM members and staff, especially with respect to visiting and monitoring capacities (Benin, Niger, Togo), torture prevention (Niger), as well as specific issues of concern, such as monitoring of violence against LGBTI persons in detention (Peru).

target.value: At least 15 training activities and workshops executed, at least two study visits/peer learning activities conducted, tools on understanding on international standards on torture prevention developed and replicated, monitoring visits to places of detention conducted in at least four countries.

actual.value: Over 18 training and capacity building activities and workshops provided in inter alia Burkina Faso, Gabon, Honduras, Mauritania, Maldives, Mexico, Togo, Tunisia, Benin, Moldova, Niger and Ukraine.

title.narrative: Laws (or revisions thereon) on NPMs were drafted, discussed and advocated among relevant stakeholders, adopted and promulgated in accordance with OPCAT, operational efficiency of NPMs was improved through adoption of strategic plans, guidelines and other tools.
Number of laws/legislative changes initiated and adopted, in compliance with the OPCAT; number or strategic plans, guidelines etc. adopted.

target.value: At least two draft laws or decrees on NPM’s establishment drafted and/or adopted; at least three visit methodology and strategic plans improved, operational tools (database, platform, electronic report, guide, infographic) and guidelines of NPM developed/revised/adopted in at least five countries.

actual.value: Legislative reforms and advocacy were supported by at least three projects and supported drafting of three decrees/law on NPM establishment or revision to ensure compliance with OPCAT. In Burkina Faso, the project includes revision of a decree establishing national human rights commission (NHRI) to ensure independence of the national preventive mechanism. The project in Gabon supports the final stages of NPM establishment and designation. Projects enabled set up or improved standard operating procedures or institutional set-up of NPMs (Burkina Faso, Gabon) and visiting methodology (Honduras, Maldives, Peru) in at least five countries.

target.value: At least two draft laws or decrees on NPM’s establishment drafted and/or adopted, at least three visit methodology and strategic plans improved, operational tools (database, platform, electronic report, guide, infographic) and guidelines of NPM developed/revised/adopted in at least five countries.

actual.value: The project in South Africa contributes to the improvement of the institutional setting of national preventive mechanism (composed of several institutions) to comply with the Optional Protocol. The project in Kazakhstan promoted changes in legislation and practice aimed at improving conditions in prisons, including analysis of legislation on compliance with the Nelson Mandela Rules. Projects enabled development of strategic plans (Kazakhstan – a strategy on follow-up, implementation of recommendations) and visiting methodology (Peru), guidelines and operations tools, information manuals, infographics (Chile, Uruguay), and database (Chile) in at least seven countries
